items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: it was when I played the movement from the Mozart horn concerto with my high school orchestra

ctx.x: A little. When I was in high school I was taking some classical French horn lessons with a local guy that was a couple of towns over and who was quite young himself so he was really encouraging and nice and wonderful. And so I did, I just looked at my – I was

opening boxes and trying to throw away – you know about this from moving – throwing away stuff – throwing away stuff, throwing away throwing away. And I opened up a box and there was a program from I think it was May 1975, so that’s 50 years plus a couple of months, and it was when I played the movement from the Mozart horn concerto with my high school orchestra. And that was a sweet memory. But that was the pinnacle of my classical career. I played in local – like the South Orange Symphony, and this is we’re…
You know our younger daughter played French horn for quite a few years. And I can recall listening to her, you know, when she was starting. And you described the French horn as “slippery.”
